title: Product-ideal comparison for algebraic-space blowups
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Open and closed immersions mean representable morphisms whose scheme base changes have the indicated property [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme; it is quasi-separated if its absolute diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests. Morphism properties use [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. For a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_T$ on the small etale site [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], using tensor pullback [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], write $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K}T$ for the relative Proj of $\bigoplus_{d\geq0}\mathcal K^d$, constructed by etale descent of the ordinary scheme blowups [def-nagata-global-blowup] on affine etale charts. Finite type means locally generated by finitely many sections. Let $T$ be an algebraic space and let $\mathcal I,\mathcal H\subseteq\mathcal O_T$ be finite-type quasi-coherent ideals. Put $p:T_1=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}T\to T$, $\mathcal H_1=\operatorname{im}(p^*\mathcal H\to\mathcal O_{T_1})$, and $q:T_2=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal H_1}T_1\to T_1$. There is a canonical isomorphism over $T$ $$e:T_2\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I\mathcal H}T$$ satisfying $b_{\mathcal I\mathcal H}\circ e=p\circ q$, where $b_{\mathcal I\mathcal H}$ is the blowup structure map. Here the product ideal is the image of multiplication $\mathcal I\otimes_{\mathcal O_T}\mathcal H\to\mathcal O_T$. No quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness, reducedness, or density hypothesis on $T$ is required.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal L^h=\operatorname{im}(h^*\mathcal L\to\mathcal O)$ for extension of an ideal. Pullback preserves quasi-coherence [lem-sfb-space-module-pullback-quasicoherent], and images and tensors are computed on affine etale charts [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-affine-chart-calculus]. The image of any finite local generating family generates the extended ideal; the pairwise products of two finite generating families generate their product. Thus $\mathcal H_1$ and $\mathcal I\mathcal H$ are finite-type quasi-coherent ideals. The tensor-composition formula of [lem-trf-space-chart-adjunction-tensor-realization], $a\otimes(b\otimes m)\mapsto a h^\sharp(b)\otimes m$, shows $(\mathcal L^h)^k=\mathcal L^{hk}$. Multiplication of these local representatives also gives $(\mathcal L\mathcal M)^h=\mathcal L^h\mathcal M^h$: both ideals are locally generated by the products $h^\sharp(l)h^\sharp(m)$. Put $f=pq$, $c:Y=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I\mathcal H}T\to T$, $E=\mathcal I^p$, $A=\mathcal I^f=E^q$ and $D=\mathcal H^f=\mathcal H_1^q$.

By [lem-sfb-space-blowup-chart-properties], $E$ is etale locally generated by a non-zero-divisor. Choose affine etale charts $V\to T_1$. That node identifies $T_2\times_{T_1}V\to V$ with the ordinary scheme blowup of $\mathcal H_1|_V$. These are an etale scheme cover of $T_2$, by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Apply [lemma-nagata-cartier-total-transform-blowup] on each $V$: the extension of the Cartier ideal $E|_V$ to this scheme blowup is Cartier. Hence $A$ is etale locally generated by a non-zero-divisor. Also $D$ is the exceptional ideal of $q$, so [lem-sfb-space-blowup-chart-properties] gives the same property for $D$.

source.place: Tag 085Y, first paragraph; Tag 085X (lemma-blow-up-pullback-effective-Cartier), reduced to the scheme version Tag 0809 on etale charts.

proof.text: On a common etale refinement write $A=(a)$ and $D=(d)$ with $a,d$ non-zero-divisors. Their product is $(ad)$, and $adx=0$ implies $dx=0$, then $x=0$. Thus $(\mathcal I\mathcal H)^f=AD$ is an effective Cartier ideal. Apply [lem-sfb-space-blowup-universal-property] to the center $\mathcal I\mathcal H$ and the map $f$: it gives the unique $T$-morphism $e:T_2\to Y$, with $ce=f$.

The extended ideal $(\mathcal I\mathcal H)^c=\mathcal I^c\mathcal H^c$ is Cartier by [lem-sfb-space-blowup-chart-properties]. On each affine etale scheme chart of $Y$, these are ordinary quasi-coherent ideals by [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-affine-chart-calculus]. Apply [lemma-nagata-invertible-product-factor] to these two ideal sheaves: each factor is Cartier. This means exactly that $\mathcal I^c$ and $\mathcal H^c$ are etale locally generated by non-zero-divisors. The universal property first gives $r:Y\to T_1$ with $pr=c$. Since $\mathcal H_1^r=\mathcal H^{pr}=\mathcal H^c$, it next gives $d:Y\to T_2$ with $qd=r$. In particular $fd=c$.

Both $ed$ and $\operatorname{id}_Y$ are $T$-endomorphisms of $Y$, since $ced=fd=c$. Uniqueness in [lem-sfb-space-blowup-universal-property] for $c$ and its Cartier center gives $ed=\operatorname{id}_Y$. Next $p(re)=ce=f=pq$; because $\mathcal I^f=A$ is Cartier, uniqueness for $p$ gives $re=q$. Consequently $qde=re=q$. Finally $\mathcal H_1^q=D$ is Cartier, so uniqueness for $q$ gives $de=\operatorname{id}_{T_2}$. Thus $e$ is the required isomorphism over $T$, with inverse $d$. These uniqueness statements also show that the construction is canonical, independent of the charts used to verify the Cartier conditions.

Live and side-live still have the item unsplit, there is no repair note and no live duplicate. Steps: (1) finite type and quasi-coherence come from 03GA and the chart-calculus node; transitivity of extended ideals comes from the tensor-composition formula. (2) E and D are Cartier by the exceptional-ideal clause; T2 restricted to an affine étale chart V of T1 is the scheme blowup by the flat-base-change clause; the charts cover T2 by fibre-products-etale-covers; the scheme lemma lemma-nagata-cartier-total-transform-blowup (true by the 0809 algebra) is used only on scheme charts. (3) A product of non-zero-divisors is a non-zero-divisor, so the new node gives e. (4) The scheme lemma lemma-nagata-invertible-product-factor, applied on chart-calculus charts, gives r and then d, using H1^r = H^c. (5) All three uses of uniqueness are over the right base: ed = id over c; re = q via the Cartier ideal I^f = A; de = id via the Cartier ideal H1^q = D. This writes out the inverse check that 085Y omits. The new node is statement-only, self-contained, sourced to 085U, has five real searches of all three kinds, has no space-level duplicate (only scheme-level 0806 relatives with extra hypotheses), and does not restate a parent clause. I tested it on the unit, zero, nilpotent and empty cases, and the item on zero ideals, I = O and empty T. The two nagata lemmas are Lean-closed, so they are tools. I accept both declared tool_uses (tensor composition; étale covers pull back) as generic sk-i-curve-zero foundations. lean.statement: theorem existsUnique_blowupPresentation_product_iso {S : Scheme.{u}} (T : AlgebraicSpace S) (I H : QuasiCoherentIdeal T) (hI : (I.val : T.Modules).IsFiniteType) (hH : (H.val : T.Modules).IsFiniteType) (B : BlowupPresentation I) : ∃ (H₁ : QuasiCoherentIdeal B.space) (L : QuasiCoherentIdeal T), (∃ a : (moduleTensorPullback B.projection).obj (H.val : T.Modules) ⟶ (H₁.val : B.space.Modules), a ≫ H₁.val.arrow = idealTensorMap B.projection H ∧ PresheafOfModules.IsLocallySurjective B.space.etaleTopology a.val) ∧ (∀ V : T.EtaleSite, Set.range (L.val.arrow.val.app (op V)) = idealPowerSubsheafSections I.val.arrow (SheafOfModules.unit T.structureSheaf) (fun W ↦ Set.range (H.val.arrow.val.app (op W))) 1 V) ∧ ∀ (C : BlowupPresentation H₁) (D : BlowupPresentation L), ∃! e : C.space ≅ D.space, e.hom ≫ D.projection = C.projection ≫ B.projection
lean.note: The uniquely determined extended ideal is specified by a locally surjective factorization of idealTensorMap through its inclusion. The product is specified by the existing sieve-local idealPowerSubsheafSections, equivalently the sheaf image of tensor multiplication. The conclusion applies to every blowup presentation and gives the unique isomorphism over the base. The three added stmt_deps are existing landed definition nodes; no new definition or dependency repair is needed.
